_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-11 (later) · SkyLink — My College is complete except the MAP links.
_status: My College is finished apart from three links. Shipped today: a breakdown of what a college's waiting credit actually consists of, both funding pools with each priority's target for that college, a resources list, and your tier with the missing criteria spelled out instead of just a label. The headline finding is that the waiting credit is almost entirely one thing — basic military service credit — which makes it far easier to clear than the number suggests. Two things now need you rather than another build: the three MAP links (Malone and Pedro), and a decision about who is allowed to see a college's own page.

items.text: Twenty-five pieces of real feedback on Sierra are waiting to be read, eleven of them thumbs-down, the oldest sitting since 1 July. Measured live today — the automated test rows are excluded, and only four rows have ever been marked addressed.

You asked whether hiding groups under ten students loses useful data. Measured: it hides 320 of 436 credentials but only about 5% of students and 5% of units. So the cost is not the totals — it is that three quarters of individual credentials cannot be named. Worth deciding whether a different technique would keep the names.

Student-contact worklist, about ten minutes total: five colleges have a suggested counselling address nobody could verify (the network blocks their websites from here) — each needs about ten seconds in a browser to confirm; then fourteen colleges with no contact in MAP have a suggested one ready to send to the MAP team.

Two things here need a person, not a session: four colleges publish no usable address at all for a credit question, and the fifty-two colleges that do have a CPL Assistant were never checked for a student contact. Sessions are blocked from opening college websites, so this needs a human or a differently-connected runner.

Two things to ask the MAP team for, in one conversation: a feed of the CPL requests students submit (the one section of My College that cannot be built without it), and a durable row id for the student extract — the one we rely on today is an Access autonumber that renumbers on re-import.

Wire EACR's prescriptive layer into Supabase. It knows the local course each college most likely already teaches for a credential, which turns 'adopt CompTIA A+' into 'adopt it against the CIS-25 you already run' — on both My College and Sierra. Sam's catch, now carried three sessions.

The three MAP links are the last piece of My College. You're checking with Malone and Pedro for the right ones: where a college adopts an exhibit, where it works student records, and where it updates its contacts. Each already has a section on the page waiting for it. Paste the three URLs from your address bar once you're signed in and the next session wires them in.

Worth knowing before you talk to any college about their waiting credit: almost all of it is the same thing. Of the 64,074 units already articulated and waiting on a decision, 98.8% is credit for basic military service — mostly landing on a GE or graduation area rather than a named course. Sixty-five of the 73 colleges with any are at 100%. So it isn't hundreds of separate judgment calls, it's close to one decision applied over and over, for students who already have a DD-214 or JST on file. The page now says this. Thirty-three colleges have nothing waiting at all — that's a finished queue, not a gap.

A decision only you can make, and it blocks two things at once. Letting a college open its own page without the team phrase isn't a design change — the figures are locked at the database, so an outside visitor currently sees nothing at all. Opening it means agreeing to publish per-college student numbers and staff contact details. Separately, one of our data tables can't be locked that way even in principle (a technical limit); nothing is exposed today and the privacy rules are being applied correctly, but there's no safety net under them if a future rebuild forgets. Both want the same conversation.

The tier block now tells a college which of the five criteria it's missing. Add how far: 'you're at 3.6 of the 5 units-per-student threshold' turns a checklist into a target, and the numbers are already on the page.
